transcript.en: Good afternoon everyone.
transcript.zh: 大家下午好。

transcript.en: Well, with some of you about to go out on fieldwork, it's timely that in this afternoon's session I'll be sharing some ideas about the reasons why groups of whales and dolphins sometimes swim ashore from the sea right onto the beach and, most often, die in what are known as 'mass strandings'.
transcript.zh: 你们中的一些人即将去实地考察，是时候在今天下午的课上讲讲为什么成群的鲸鱼和海豚会从大海游上海岸，并经常死于大规模的搁浅了。

transcript.en: Unfortunately, this type of event is a frequent occurrence in some of the locations that you'll be travelling to, when sometimes the tide goes out suddenly, confusing the animals.
transcript.zh: 不幸的是，这种事情经常发生在你去游览的地方。有时，那里的潮汐突然退去会使动物感到困惑。

transcript.en: However, there are many other theories about the causes of mass strandings.
transcript.zh: 然而，还有许多其他关于大规模搁浅成因的理论。

transcript.en: The first is that the behavior is linked to parasites.
transcript.zh: 首先是这种行为与寄生虫有关。

transcript.en: It's often found that stranded animals were infested with large numbers of parasites.
transcript.zh: 经常发现搁浅的动物受到大量寄生虫的感染。

transcript.en: For instance, a type of worm is commonly found in the ears of dead whales.
transcript.zh: 例如，一种虫子经常能在死鲸鱼的耳朵里找到。

transcript.en: Since marine animals rely heavily on their hearing to navigate, this type of infestation has the potential to be very harmful.
transcript.zh: 由于海洋动物主要靠听力导航，这种感染的潜在危害很大。

transcript.en: Another theory is related to toxins, or poisons.
transcript.zh: 另一种理论与毒素或毒药有关。

transcript.en: These have also been found to contribute to the death of many marine animals.
transcript.zh: 这些也导致了许多海洋生物的死亡。

transcript.en: Many toxins, as I'm sure you're aware, originate from plants, or animals.
transcript.zh: 我想你们也知道，许多毒素来源于植物和动物。

transcript.en: The whale ingests these toxins in its normal feeding behavior but whether these poisons directly or indirectly lead to stranding and death, seems to depend upon the toxin involved.
transcript.zh: 鲸鱼在它们的日常摄食行为中摄取了这些毒素，但是这些毒药是否直接或间接导致搁浅和死亡似乎要取决于涉及的毒素本身。

transcript.en: In 1988, for example, fourteen humpback whales examined after stranding along the beaches of Cape Cod were found to have been poisoned after eating tuna that contained saxitoxin, the same toxin that can be fatal in humans.
transcript.zh: 例如，1988 年，在科德角海滩搁浅的 14 头座头鲸经检查后发现，它们是因为食用了含有蛤蚌毒素（这种毒素对人类也可能是致命的）的金枪鱼而中毒的。

transcript.en: Alternatively, it has also been suggested that some animals strand accidentally by following their prey ashore in the confusion of the chase.
transcript.zh: 另外，也有人提出，一些动物是在追捕猎物时陷入混乱，跟着猎物上岸，从而意外搁浅的。

transcript.en: In 1995 David Thurston monitored pilot whales that beached after following the squid ashore.
transcript.zh: 1995年，大卫·瑟斯顿监控到巨头鲸在追踪岸边的鱿鱼后搁浅。

transcript.en: However, this idea does not seem to hold true for the majority of mass strandings because examination of the animals' stomach contents reveal that most had not been feeding as they stranded.
transcript.zh: 然而，这种想法并不适用于大多数大规模的搁浅，因为当检查搁浅的动物时，发现多数动物的胃里没有食物。

transcript.en: There are also some new theories, which link strandings to humans.
transcript.zh: 还有一些新理论将搁浅与人类相连。

transcript.en: A growing concern is that loud noises in the ocean cause strandings.
transcript.zh: 海洋噪音引发搁浅日益受到人们的关注。

transcript.en: Noises such as these caused by military exercises are of particular concern and have been pinpointed as the cause of some strandings of late.
transcript.zh: 例如军事演习的噪音特别受到关注，而且作为一些搁浅的原因被指出。

transcript.en: One of these, a mass stranding of whales in 2000 in the Bahamas coincided closely with experiments using a new submarine detection system.
transcript.zh: 其中一个发生在2000年的巴哈马群岛，一次大规模的鲸鱼搁浅与新型水下探测系统的实验同时发生。

transcript.en: There were several factors that made this stranding stand out as different from previous strandings.
transcript.zh: 有一些因素表明这次搁浅与以往的搁浅不同。

transcript.en: This led researchers to look for a new cause.
transcript.zh: 这让研究人员开始寻找新的原因。

transcript.en: For one, all the stranded animals were healthy.
transcript.zh: 首先，所有搁浅的动物都很健康。

transcript.en: In addition, the animals were spread out along 38 kilometers of coast, whereas it's more common for the animals to be found in a group when mass strandings occur.
transcript.zh: 另外，动物在海岸上散布了38公里，然而当大规模搁浅发生时，动物往往是成群的被发现。

transcript.en: A final theory is related to group behaviour, and suggests that sea mammals cannot distinguish between sick and healthy leaders and will follow sick leaders, even to an inevitable death.
transcript.zh: 最后一个理论与团体行为有关，海洋哺乳动物不能区分生病和健康的领导者，它们会跟随患病的领导者，即使是导致一场不可避免的死亡。

transcript.en: This is a particularly interesting theory since the whales that are thought to be most social - the toothed whales - are the group that strand the most frequently.
transcript.zh: 这是一个很有意思的理论，因为鲸鱼（齿鲸）被认为是最爱群居的动物，它们最频繁的成群搁浅

transcript.en: The theory is also supported by evidence from a dolphin stranding in 1994. Examination of the dead animals revealed that apart from the leader, all the others had been healthy at the time of their death.
transcript.zh: 1994年海豚的搁浅也证实了这个理论。检查动物的死尸时发现，除了领导者以外，其他所有动物在死时都很健康。

transcript.en: Without one consistent theory however it is very hard for us to do anything about this phenomenon except to assist animal where and when we can.
transcript.zh: 然而，没有一个统一的理论很难让我们改变这个现象，除了帮助那些我们在何时何地发现的动物。

transcript.en: Stranding networks have been established around the world to aid in rescuing animals and collecting samples from those that could not be helped.
transcript.zh: 全世界成立了搁浅网络，旨在救助动物并从那些无法获救的动物身上提取样本。

transcript.en: I recommend John Connor's Marine Mammals ashore as an excellent starting point if you're interested in finding out more about these networks, or establishing one yourself.
transcript.zh: 如果你们想找到更多这方面的网络或建立自己的网络，我推荐约翰·康纳的“海洋哺乳动物上岸”作为一个极好的出发点。
